note: The one source of truth for which skills exist and when each switches on. The tables in SKILL.md, AGENTS.md and docs/agents.md, the routing block and the session start note are generated from this file: run `mstack.py catalog --write` after changing it.

skills.name: ping-me
skills.when: You need the person's decision or input, or a task they asked for is complete or blocked. On by default: notify them without being asked.

skills.name: outcome-first
skills.when: Any task bigger than a few steps: pin the outcome, ask every question in one batch with defaults, then run to a verified outcome without further input.

skills.name: multi-evaluator
skills.when: Someone wants a product's design reviewed and improved in rounds by independent AI reviewers from different makers until it is ready for real people (every journey 9 or better, reviewers agreeing, no high fix open, two rounds running).

skills.name: design-direction
skills.when: Someone wants to find the look of a new product, choose between design directions, or make on-brand variants to pick from: up to four whole working directions from one brief, a comparison page with a recommendation, the person's pick, structure-only variants with numbered questions, then a locked brand file.

skills.name: away-mode
skills.when: You are about to present a file, report, mockup, screenshot or link, or the person says they are on their phone, away, out or back. Notice when they are away and deliver phone-readable copies (PNG, PDF, files in the chat, key points in the reply).

skills.name: crew
skills.when: The person wants work to carry on in the background while they are away or asleep, within the usage they already pay for: a queue across every project on the cheapest fitting model, 15% of every usage window kept for them, drafts and side branches only, one morning digest. Also "what did the crew finish" and "what is my usage".

skills.name: mstack
skills.when: The person asks what is happening across their projects, wants a brief for another agent or a rules file for a project, switches a skill off or on, asks to "review my skills", or an mStack skill has just finished.

commands.use_when: The person asks what is happening across all their projects or what is waiting on them.
The person asks for a brief for a tester, reviewer, worker, researcher or security check they are about to start.
The person wants a rules file for a project, or the same rules carried into every brief.
The person says to switch a skill off for good (`enable <skill>` switches it back on). For one task, just do not use it.
The person asks to "review my skills", what their skills have learned, or to improve a skill.
After any mStack skill finishes: record privately how it went.
The person wants mStack set up in Codex, Cursor (`setup cursor`) or Claude Code hooks (`setup claude-hooks`).
